title: “Please, Sir, I Want Some More": The Truth About Victorian Workhouses
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的面向求知欲旺盛的英语学习者的播客节目，在这里你可以听到引人入胜的故事，了解世界上光怪陆离而又精彩绝伦的事物，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the Victorian workhouse, the 19th century institution which housed the most desperate people in Britain.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们将要聊一聊维多利亚时期的济贫院，这个 19 世纪的机构曾收容了英国最走投无路的人。

sentences.en: We'll learn why they were created, what life was really like inside them, hear some shocking stories, and learn how they were replaced by the welfare state we have today.
sentences.zh: 我们将了解它们建立的原因、里面的真实生活是什么样的、听一些令人震惊的故事，并了解它们后来是如何被我们今天的福利国家制度所取代的。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们就废话少说，直接切入正题。

sentences.en: It is the winter of 1837. A small boy stands in a large stone hall.
sentences.zh: 那是 1837 年的冬天。一个瘦小的男孩站在宽大的石头大厅里。

sentences.en: Around him, other children sit in rows, hunched over their bowls.
sentences.zh: 在他周围，其他孩子一排排地坐着，身体佝偻在各自的碗上。

sentences.en: The meal is gruel, which is water with a little oatmeal stirred into it.
sentences.zh: 饭是粥，也就是水里面搅了一点燕麦片。

sentences.en: It's the same meal every day, which the boys devour out of necessity.
sentences.zh: 每天都是同样的饭菜，男孩们出于饥饿狼吞虎咽地吃光了。

sentences.en: The portions are measly, and their stomachs are again rumbling minutes after they have finished eating.
sentences.zh: 饭量少得可怜，他们刚吃完饭几分钟，肚子就又咕咕叫了起来。

sentences.en: One boy walks up to the master, nervously.
sentences.zh: 一个男孩紧张地走到主管跟前。

sentences.en: He holds out his bowl. "Please, sir," he says.
sentences.zh: 他伸出自己的碗。“请，先生，”他说。

sentences.en: "I want some more." The master cannot believe the request.
sentences.zh: “我还想要点。”主管简直不敢相信这个要求。

sentences.en: "What?", he asks, before declaring that the boy will be hanged one day.
sentences.zh: “什么？”他问道，接着断言这个男孩有一天会被绞死。

sentences.en: You may recognise this as the start of Charles Dickens' Oliver Twist.
sentences.zh: 你可能认出这是 Charles Dickens 的《Oliver Twist》的开头。

sentences.en: That image, this of a small, frightened, starving child asking for a little more food, became one of the most famous in English literature.
sentences.zh: 这个画面——一个瘦小、惊恐、饥饿的孩子要求再多吃一点食物——成为了英国文学中最著名的画面之一。

sentences.en: The location for this scene was of course the workhouse, Victorian Britain's answer to the question of what to do with the poorest in society.
sentences.zh: 这个场景发生的地方当然就是济贫院，维多利亚时代的英国对于如何安置社会中最贫困人口这一问题的解答。

sentences.en: Now, to understand where workhouses come from, we need to go back a few hundred years to talk about how the British state dealt with the poorest people in society.
sentences.zh: 现在，要理解济贫院的来历，我们需要回到几百年前，谈谈英国国家是如何处理社会中最贫困的人口的。

sentences.en: The short answer is it didn't. For much of British history, if you were unable to work and support yourself, tough luck.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是，它没有。在英国历史的很大一部分时间里，如果你无法工作并养活自己，那就只能自求多福了。

sentences.en: You'd be reduced to begging, perhaps pushed into prostitution, or to relying on the charity of others.
sentences.zh: 你会被迫去乞讨，也许会被迫卖淫，或者依靠他人的慈善救济。

sentences.en: This was improved slightly in 1601, under Elizabeth I, when a law was passed that made parishes — the groups of local churches — they were responsible for looking after the extreme poor in the local area.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在 1601 年伊丽莎白一世统治时期得到了轻微的改善，当时通过了一项法律，规定教区（地方教会组织）负责照顾当地极度贫困的人。

sentences.en: If you were destitute, you could apply for what was called outdoor relief, which was a small amount of money or food to help you survive in your own home.
sentences.zh: 如果你一无所有，你可以申请所谓的“户外救济”，这是一小笔钱或食物，用来帮助你在自己家里存活下来。

sentences.en: This was later expanded to even include the working poor, whereby parishes topped up the wages of underpaid workers to ensure that they had enough money to support their families.
sentences.zh: 后来，这一范围甚至扩大到了贫穷的工人阶级，教区以此来补贴薪水过低的工人，以确保他们有足够的钱养家糊口。

sentences.en: It was imperfect. It was inconsistent, and it varied from parish to parish, from one area to the next.
sentences.zh: 它并不完美。它前后不一，并且因教区而异，从一个地区到另一个地区各不相同。

sentences.en: But it allowed people to remain with their families in their own homes.
sentences.zh: 但它允许人们和家人一起留在自己的家中。

sentences.en: The problem, as the politicians and economists of the time saw it, was it was too easy to get.
sentences.zh: 当时的政客和经济学家认为，问题在于这种救济太容易得到了。

sentences.en: It was, in their view, encouraging the poor to stay poor.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，这助长了穷人安于贫困的心理。

sentences.en: If you could receive a little money without working, why would you bother working?
sentences.zh: 如果你不工作就能拿到一点钱，你为什么还要费力去工作呢？

sentences.en: On the other side of the coin, it was also, they said, letting employers get away with paying low wages because they knew that their workers would receive top-ups from the parish.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他们说，这也让雇主得以支付低工资，因为他们知道工人们会得到教区的补贴。

sentences.en: And there was an ever increasing number of people in Britain who were forced to turn to this, either to request top-ups of their low wages, or who had fallen into destitution.
sentences.zh: 英国有越来越多的人被迫转向这种方式，要么是要求补贴低工资，要么是已经陷入赤贫。

sentences.en: By the early 19th century, Britain’s population had more than doubled, growing from six and a half million to fourteen million in just eighty years.
sentences.zh: 到 19 世纪初，英国的人口已经翻了一番多，在短短八十年里从六百五十万增长到了一千四百万。

sentences.en: The industrial revolution had transformed the economy.
sentences.zh: 工业革命改变了经济。

sentences.en: Factories had replaced cottage industries.
sentences.zh: 工厂取代了家庭手工业。

sentences.en: Millions of people flooded from the countryside to the cities in search of work.
sentences.zh: 数百万农村人口涌入城市寻找工作。

sentences.en: In these cities, places like Manchester, Birmingham, and London, work was irregular, housing was cramped and expensive, and millions of people were just a hair's breadth away from absolute destitution.
sentences.zh: 在这些城市里，比如曼彻斯特、伯明翰和伦敦，工作极不稳定，住房拥挤且昂贵，数百万人距离绝对赤贫只有一线之隔。

sentences.en: The old structures of local charity and parish relief were never designed for this, and were creaking under the demand.
sentences.zh: 地方慈善和教区救济的旧体制从来就不是为了应对这种局面而设计的，在巨大的需求下摇摇欲坠。

sentences.en: Between 1780 and 1831, the cost of poor relief in England and Wales had roughly quadrupled, gone up four times.
sentences.zh: 在 1780 年到 1831 年之间，英格兰和威尔士的济贫救济成本大约翻了两番，增长了四倍。

sentences.en: The money was going out, but the problem kept growing.
sentences.zh: 钱花出去了，但问题却越来越严重。

sentences.en: So, in 1832, a Royal Commission was set up to investigate.
sentences.zh: 因此，在 1832 年，成立了一个皇家委员会来进行调查。

sentences.en: Its key architect was a man named Edwin Chadwick, who was a follower of the philosopher Jeremy Bentham.
sentences.zh: 它的主要策划者是一个名叫 Edwin Chadwick 的人，他是哲学家 Jeremy Bentham 的追随者。

sentences.en: As such, he believed in systems, in efficiency, in the idea that human behaviour could be shaped by designing the right incentives.
sentences.zh: 因此，他信仰体制、信仰效率，坚信可以通过设计正确的激励机制来塑造人类行为。

sentences.en: The Commission's report came back with a series of suggestions about what to do about poverty, which were put into law with the Poor Law Amendment of 1834.
sentences.zh: 委员会的报告提出了关于如何解决贫困问题的一系列建议，并通过 1834 年的《济贫法修正案》变成了法律。

sentences.en: And specifically, in terms of what we're talking about today, this led directly to the institutionalisation of the workhouse.
sentences.zh: 具体就我们今天讨论的内容而言，这直接导致了济贫院的制度化。

sentences.en: Now, workhouses were not a new invention.
sentences.zh: 其实，济贫院并不是什么新发明。

sentences.en: They had existed in various forms since the early 1700s as places where the destitute could go to receive food and shelter in exchange for work.
sentences.zh: 早在 18 世纪初，它们就以各种形式存在了，是赤贫者可以去那里以工作换取食物和住所的地方。

sentences.en: But they were patchy. Inconsistently run.
sentences.zh: 但它们参差不齐。管理很不规范。

sentences.en: They varied enormously from one parish to the next.
sentences.zh: 不同教区之间的情况差异巨大。

sentences.en: What the 1834 Act did was take this existing idea and transform it.
sentences.zh: 1834 年的法案所做的，是将这个现有的想法拿来并加以改造。

sentences.en: Every area of England and Wales would now have a workhouse.
sentences.zh: 英格兰和威尔士的每一个地区现在都将拥有一座济贫院。

sentences.en: Every workhouse would operate on the same national principles.
sentences.zh: 每个济贫院都将按照相同的国家原则运作。

sentences.en: And those principles would be deliberately, intentionally harsh.
sentences.zh: 而这些原则将是蓄意的、故意地严厉。

sentences.en: At the heart of this was a principle with a rather cold name: " less eligibility."
sentences.zh: 这的核心是一个听起来相当冰冷的原则：“劣等处遇原则（less eligibility）”。

sentences.en: The conditions inside a workhouse must be worse than the conditions of the lowest independent labourer outside it.
sentences.zh: 济贫院内部的条件必须比外面最底层自食其力的劳工的条件还要糟糕。

sentences.en: In other words, however bad it might be working the worst possible job that paid you the least possible salary, life in the workhouse needed to be worse.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，无论做报酬最少的最糟糕工作有多么糟糕，济贫院里的生活也必须更糟糕。

sentences.en: The logic was that it needed to be a genuine deterrent, which only the truly destitute would turn to.
sentences.zh: 其逻辑在于，它需要成为一种真正的震慑，只有真正赤贫的人才会求助于它。

sentences.en: The state would help in this case, but it would make absolutely certain you did not want to be there.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下国家会提供帮助，但它会绝对确保你打心底里不想待在那里。

sentences.en: It was designed like this because it had a specific target in mind: the able-bodied man who was choosing idleness over work.
sentences.zh: 它的设计初衷是有特定目标的：那些宁愿游手好闲也不愿工作的身强力壮的男子。

sentences.en: Force him into a place unpleasant enough, so the argument went, and he would find a job.
sentences.zh: 根据这种论调，把他强行塞进一个足够令人不愉快的地方，他就会去找工作了。

sentences.en: But the majority of people who actually ended up inside the workhouse were not idle young men.
sentences.zh: 但实际上最终落入济贫院的大多数人并非游手好闲的年轻男子。

sentences.en: The majority were the elderly, who had outlived their ability to earn a living.
sentences.zh: 大多数是老年人，他们的寿命已经超出了他们谋生的能力。

sentences.en: They were the chronically sick, who could not work because of illness or disability.
sentences.zh: 他们是长期生病的慢性病人，因疾病或残疾而无法工作。

sentences.en: They were children, many of them orphans.
sentences.zh: 他们是儿童，其中许多是孤儿。

sentences.en: And they were women: pregnant women, unmarried mothers, widows, or women whose husbands had abandoned them.
sentences.zh: 他们是女性：孕妇、未婚母亲、寡妇，或是被丈夫抛弃的妇女。

sentences.en: There were about 600 workhouses across England and Wales, with an estimated 150,000 people living in them at any one point.
sentences.zh: 英格兰和威尔士大约有 600 家济贫院，在任何一个时间点，估计都有 15 万人住在里面。

sentences.en: And life inside, well, it was incredibly grim.
sentences.zh: 至于里面的生活，嗯，简直阴暗得难以置信。

sentences.en: Men and women were separate. Children were separated from parents, brothers from sisters.
sentences.zh: 男女分开关押。孩子与父母分离，兄弟与姐妹分离。

sentences.en: Their clothes would be taken away, to be replaced by a rough grey uniform.
sentences.zh: 他们的衣服会被收走，换上粗糙的灰色制服。

sentences.en: The diet inside was set by a national schedule.
sentences.zh: 里面的饮食由国家统一安排。

sentences.en: Breakfast was gruel, every morning. Lunch was bread and perhaps a little cheese.
sentences.zh: 早餐是粥，每天早晨都一样。午餐是面包和一点点奶酪。

sentences.en: In the evening, a thin broth, or very occasionally a small portion of cooked meat.
sentences.zh: 晚上是一碗稀薄的肉汤，偶尔极少有一小份煮熟的肉。

sentences.en: Suet pudding might appear once or twice a week.
sentences.zh: 羊脂布丁可能会一周出现一两次。

sentences.en: And as for the quantities, they were calculated to be just enough to stop you dying of hunger, but nothing more.
sentences.zh: 至于分量，计算得刚刚好让你不至于饿死，仅此而已。

sentences.en: And no, you certainly couldn't ask for a second helping.
sentences.zh: 而且不，你绝对不能要求来第二份。

sentences.en: And when you weren't eating your meagre rations of food, you were working, long hours doing hard, tedious work.
sentences.zh: 当你不用吃那些微薄的口粮时，你就在工作，长时间地从事又重又枯燥的工作。

sentences.en: One of the most common tasks given to women and children was unpicking old rope, separating the fibres so it could be used again.
sentences.zh: 分派给妇女和儿童最常见的任务之一是拆解旧绳索，把纤维拆散以便重新使用。

sentences.en: You had to use your bare fingers, and it was slow, relentless work.
sentences.zh: 你必须用光秃秃的手指去撕扯，这是一项缓慢而无情的工作。

sentences.en: Your fingertips would crack and bleed. And it never ended.
sentences.zh: 你的指尖会开裂、流血。而且永无止境。

sentences.en: Once you finished one piece of rope, there was always another to be done.
sentences.zh: 一旦你拆完了一段绳索，总有另一段等着你去干。

sentences.en: Men were often set to breaking stones to lay on roads, or to grinding bones that would be used as fertiliser.
sentences.zh: 男人们通常被派去敲碎石头铺路，或是研磨用作肥料的骨头。

sentences.en: Or perhaps to working the treadmill, which was a large paddle wheel that you climbed continuously for hours at a time.
sentences.zh: 或者也许是去踩跑步机，那是一个大型的脚踏轮，你需要连续爬上好几个小时。

sentences.en: The treadmill had originally been used to pump water or grind grain.
sentences.zh: 跑步机最初是用来抽水或磨谷物的。

sentences.en: But by this period, in many workhouses, it served no productive purpose at all.
sentences.zh: 但在这一时期，在许多济贫院里，它根本没有任何生产用途。

sentences.en: It was used simply because it was exhausting and unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 使用它纯粹是因为它令人精疲力竭且极不愉快。

sentences.en: In terms of the architecture of these workhouses, many were built around the same principles of order and control that you have in prisons, where guards can stand in the centre and observe what everyone is doing.
sentences.zh: 就这些济贫院的建筑风格而言，许多都是围绕着监狱中那种秩序和控制的原则建造的，守卫可以站在中央观察每个人的举动。

sentences.en: Open dormitories. Shared dining halls with long, visible sight lines.
sentences.zh: 开放式宿舍。共享的餐厅，视线长且一览无余。

sentences.en: A layout built around the idea that the master and matron could see everything, and that inmates knew there was nowhere to hide.
sentences.zh: 这种布局的建立是基于这样的理念：主管和女管家可以看到一切，而囚禁者知道无处可藏。

sentences.en: Importantly, it wasn't a prison. You could leave, in theory.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，它不是监狱。理论上你是可以离开的。

sentences.en: But you had to give notice, and in many cases wait twenty-four hours before being discharged.
sentences.zh: 但你必须提前通知，并且在许多情况下需要等待二十四小时才能被释放。

sentences.en: And more importantly, you left with nothing: no money, no food, nothing to support you in the outside world.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，你离开时一无所有：没有钱，没有食物，没有任何东西能在外部世界支撑你。

sentences.en: For the elderly, the chronically ill, and the very young, there was often nowhere else to go.
sentences.zh: 对于老年人、慢性病患者和极幼小的儿童来说，往往无处可去。

sentences.en: They entered, they stayed, and in many cases, they died there.
sentences.zh: 他们进去了，住下了，在许多情况下，他们就死在了那里。

sentences.en: And the conditions inside were no secret; everyone knew what lay behind those gates, and most people did everything they possibly could to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 里面的条件并不是什么秘密；每个人都知道那些大门后面是什么，大多数人都竭尽全力去避免它。

sentences.en: Yet in some workhouses, the reality was worse than anyone imagined.
sentences.zh: 然而在某些济贫院里，现实比任何人想象的还要糟糕。

sentences.en: In 1845, a small item appeared in a local Hampshire newspaper.
sentences.zh: 1845 年，汉普郡的一家地方报纸上出现了一则简短的新闻。

sentences.en: It concerned the workhouse in the market town of Andover, in southern England.
sentences.zh: 它关乎英格兰南部集镇安多弗（Andover）的济贫院。

sentences.en: Its inmates were mostly agricultural labourers, men and women who had worked the land their whole lives and had fallen into destitution when work dried up, or when illness or injury made them unable to continue.
sentences.zh: 里面的 inmates（院民）大多是农业短工，这些男男女女一生都在耕作土地，当工作枯竭，或者疾病和伤残使他们无以为继时，便陷入了赤贫。

sentences.en: They had been set to work grinding bones.
sentences.zh: 他们被派去研磨骨头。

sentences.en: Old animal bones, mostly horse bones, collected from farms and slaughterhouses.
sentences.zh: 旧的动物骨头，主要是马骨，从农场和屠宰场收集而来。

sentences.en: You reduced them to powder using a heavy metal rod, and the powder was sold as fertiliser.
sentences.zh: 你用一根沉重的金属棒把它们砸成粉末，然后这些粉末被当作肥料出售。

sentences.en: The newspaper report alleged that the inmates were so hungry that they were fighting over the bones before they ground them.
sentences.zh: 报纸报道称，院民们饿得在骨头研磨之前就开始争抢它们。

sentences.en: They were biting and gnawing at them. Sucking out the marrow.
sentences.zh: 他们用牙齿去咬、去啃。吮吸骨髓。

sentences.en: Scraping off whatever scraps of rotting meat and gristle remained.
sentences.zh: 刮掉上面残留的任何腐烂的肉和软骨残渣。

sentences.en: The story reached London, and it was a scandal.
sentences.zh: 这个故事传到了伦敦，引起了轩然大波。

sentences.en: These were not starving people outside the system.
sentences.zh: 这些不是体制外的饥民。

sentences.en: These were starving people inside it, being theoretically cared for by the state.
sentences.zh: 而是体制内的饥民，理论上是由国家照顾的人。

sentences.en: A parliamentary committee was set up. And what it found was worse than the newspaper had suggested.
sentences.zh: 成立了一个议会调查委员会。而它的调查结果比报纸暗示的还要糟糕。

sentences.en: The master of the Andover workhouse was a man named Colin McDougal, a former army sergeant.
sentences.zh: 安多弗济贫院的主管是一个名叫 Colin McDougal 的人，曾是一名陆军中士。

sentences.en: He had been, the committee found, habitually drunk.
sentences.zh: 调查委员会发现，他经常酗酒。

sentences.en: He had been brutal towards inmates, using physical violence against men and women, and sexually abusing the women.
sentences.zh: 他对院民非常残暴，对男女使用暴力，并对女性进行性虐待。

sentences.en: One witness testified that the inmates had been so hungry that when a horse died in the yard, they had been grateful, because it meant more bones to grind, and more scraps to fight over.
sentences.zh: 一位证人作证说，院民们饿得实在没办法，当院子里有一匹马死掉时，他们竟然心存感激，因为这意味着有更多的骨头可以磨，有更多的残渣可以争抢。

sentences.en: A woman testified that she had been too frightened to report anything, because to report the master was to risk punishment, and in the workhouse, the master controlled everything: your food, your sleeping arrangements, and your ability to see your children.
sentences.zh: 一位妇女作证说，她太害怕而不敢举报任何事情，因为举报主管就意味着面临惩罚，而在济贫院里，主管控制着一切：你的食物、你的睡眠安排以及你看望孩子的权力。

sentences.en: The workhouse master was dismissed. There were some minor changes to the law.
sentences.zh: 这名济贫院主管被解雇了。法律做了一些小幅修改。

sentences.en: But the men and women of the Andover workhouse went back to grinding bones.
sentences.zh: 但安多弗济贫院的男男女女又回去研磨骨头了。

sentences.en: Now, almost from the creation of the workhouse laws, critics had been arguing that it was inhumane, unnecessarily predatory towards those who were already at rock bottom.
sentences.zh: 事实上，几乎从济贫院法律出台之日起，批评者就一直在争论说它很不人道，对那些已经跌入谷底的人来说过于掠夺性。

sentences.en: The argument for it was always that it was a deterrent, that in making the workhouse so awful you would ensure a strong incentive for people to support themselves.
sentences.zh: 支持它的理由一直是它是一种震慑，通过把济贫院变得如此可怕，你就能确保为人们自食其力提供强有力的动力。

sentences.en: Or to put it another way, if you made poverty easier and more comfortable, you would encourage it.
sentences.zh: 或者换句话说，如果你让贫困变得更容易、更舒适，你就是在助长贫困。

sentences.en: The reality is that it was an absolute last resort for practically everyone.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，对几乎所有人来说，这是绝对的最后手段。

sentences.en: You might remember a lady who was forced to send her sons to the workhouse, from an episode early this year.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得今年早些时候某一集里，有个女人被迫把儿子送进济贫院。

sentences.en: In 1896, a music hall singer had fallen on particularly hard times, and with nobody to turn to and no way to support her sons, she made the agonising decision to send them to a workhouse.
sentences.zh: 1896 年，一位音乐厅歌手遭遇了特别艰难的时期，在走投无路且无法养活儿子的情况下，她做出痛苦的决定，将他们送进了济贫院。

sentences.en: Her older son was twelve. Her younger son was seven.
sentences.zh: 她的大儿子十二岁。小儿子七岁。

sentences.en: The woman's name was Hannah, and her younger son was Charlie, Charlie Chaplin.
sentences.zh: 这个女人的名字叫 Hannah，她的小儿子就是 Charlie，Charlie Chaplin（查理·卓别林）。

sentences.en: Charlie Chaplin would later describe that morning in his autobiography.
sentences.zh: 查理·卓别林后来在他的自传中描述了那个早晨。

sentences.en: His mother had tried to keep their spirits up on the walk to the workhouse.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲在去济贫院的路上一直试图振奋他们的精神。

sentences.en: But the boys, he wrote, could sense her despair.
sentences.zh: 但他写道，孩子们能感觉到她的绝望。

sentences.en: And then, at the workhouse gates, they were parted.
sentences.zh: 然后，在济贫院大门口，他们分开了。

sentences.en: Charlie and his brother to the boys' ward.
sentences.zh: 查理和他的兄弟去了男孩病房。

sentences.en: Their mother to the women's. Chaplin said later that the humiliations of those years were what made him who he was.
sentences.zh: 他们的母亲去了女性病房。卓别林后来表示，那几年所遭受的屈辱塑造了他的人生。

sentences.en: He went on to become, by many measures, the most famous man in the world, and if you'd like to hear more about his life, episode 598 is the one for you.
sentences.zh: 后来，从许多方面来看，他成为了世界上最著名的人，如果你想听更多关于他一生的故事，第 598 集就是为你准备的。

sentences.en: Now, fortunately for Charlie he didn't stay in the workhouse forever, and the entire system itself would soon start to be dismantled.
sentences.zh: 现在，对查理来说幸运的是，他并没有永远待在济贫院里，整个系统本身也很快开始解体。

sentences.en: Reformers had been pushing for a total abolition of the workhouse system, to be replaced with proper state services for health, unemployment, and old age.
sentences.zh: 改革者们一直在极力主张彻底废除济贫院制度，代之以针对健康、失业和老龄的适当国家服务。

sentences.en: And they came eventually. Old age pensions arrived in 1908, meaning the elderly no longer had to choose between the workhouse and starvation.
sentences.zh: 而这些最终还是来了。老年养老金于 1908 年问世，这意味着老年人不再必须在济贫院和挨饿之间做出选择。

sentences.en: Then in 1911 came what was called national insurance.
sentences.zh: 然后在 1911 年出台了所谓的国民保险。

sentences.en: The idea was that workers, employers, and the government would each contribute a small amount every week to a shared fund.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，工人、雇主和政府每周各自向一个共享基金会贡献一小笔钱。

sentences.en: And if you then lost your job or fell seriously ill, you could draw from that fund.
sentences.zh: 如果你随后失业或严重生病，你就可以从该基金中支取。

sentences.en: This still exists today, by the way; if you work in the UK you'll know that every month a portion of your salary is set aside for " National Insurance contributions".
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这在今天依然存在；如果你在英国工作，你就会知道每个月你的薪水里都会有一部分被留作“国民保险缴款”。

sentences.en: It's pretty much the same thing. Now, even after the introduction of pensions and of national insurance, the workhouse remained.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一回事。然而，即使在养老金和国民保险引入之后，济贫院依然存在。

sentences.en: The reason was that neither reform was universal.
sentences.zh: 原因在于这两项改革都不是普遍适用的。

sentences.en: National insurance in 1911 only covered workers in regulated employment in specific industries.
sentences.zh: 1911 年的国民保险仅涵盖特定行业中受规管就业的工人。

sentences.en: It did not cover casual labourers, domestic servants, or the self-employed.
sentences.zh: 它不包括临时工、家政仆人或自谋职业者。

sentences.en: Old age pensions were only paid to those over seventy.
sentences.zh: 老年养老金只发放给七十岁以上的人。

sentences.en: Anyone who fell outside those categories still had no alternative to the workhouse.
sentences.zh: 任何落入这些类别之外的人仍然没有替代济贫院的选择。

sentences.en: It was not until 1948, with the National Assistance Act and the formal creation of the welfare state, that the Poor Law, and the workhouse, were finally abolished.
sentences.zh: 直到 1948 年，随着《国民援助法》的颁布和福利国家的正式建立，《济贫法》和济贫院才终于被废除。

sentences.en: Today, a pregnant single mother, an orphaned child or a man too old to work is no longer forced to ring the bell outside the workhouse gates; there are systems and safeguards in place to ensure that everyone, in theory, has the right to a dignified existence.
sentences.zh: 今天，一个怀孕的单亲妈妈、一个孤儿或一个年纪太大而无法工作的男子，再也不用被迫按响济贫院大门外的铃铛；现在有了各种系统和保障措施，以确保每个人在理论上都享有过上有尊严生活的权利。

sentences.en: Yet the discussions about how to do that are much the same as those that were going on 200 years ago.
sentences.zh: 然而，关于如何做到这一点的讨论与 200 年前进行的讨论大同小异。

sentences.en: How does a society support people who cannot support themselves, without creating a system that some politicians and taxpayers see as unfair, or that creates a disincentive to work?
sentences.zh: 一个社会如何在不建立一个被某些政客和纳税人认为是不公平的、或者会产生工作消极性的体制的前提下，去支持那些无法自食其力的人呢？

sentences.en: And how do you make that judgement when poverty is caused not only by unemployment, but by illness, old age, low wages, insecure work and high housing costs?
sentences.zh: 当贫困不仅由失业引起，还由疾病、年老、低工资、不稳定的工作和高昂的住房成本引起时，你又该如何做出这种判断？

sentences.en: Like the Royal Commission back in 1832, there are those who argue that it is now too easy to fall back on state support, and that state support is so great that there is often not much financial difference between working and not working.
sentences.zh: 就像 1832 年的皇家委员会一样，现在也有人认为，依靠国家支持变得太容易了，国家支持如此丰厚，以至于工作与不工作在经济上往往没有多大区别。

sentences.en: And of course there are plenty of people who say this is nonsense, and that these people want to work, but there simply aren't sufficient jobs for them.
sentences.zh: 当然，也有很多人说这是无稽之谈，这些人其实想工作，只是根本没有足够的工作岗位供他们选择。

sentences.en: Fortunately for everyone concerned, nobody is suggesting the revival of the workhouse.
sentences.zh: 对所有相关人员来说幸运的是，没有人建议复活济贫院。

sentences.en: That has been forever consigned to the pages of Oliver Twist.
sentences.zh: 那个已经被永远封存在《Oliver Twist》的字里行间了。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on Victorian workhouses.
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是今天关于维多利亚时期济贫院的全部内容。

sentences.en: We've made quite a few related episodes: episode number 598 on Charlie Chaplin, there's even an episode on Jeremy Bentham, which is episode number 116.
sentences.zh: 我们做过相当多的相关节目：关于查理·卓别林的第 598 集，甚至还有一集关于 Jeremy Bentham 的，也就是第 116 集。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
